prompt: A single wide horizontal panel. Down the far left edge runs a narrow grey strip where a chatbot icon takes in a question mark and emits one short sentence that dead-ends at a stop sign — one reply, then silence. The rest of the frame belongs to the agent: a small robot walking a long, winding trail through a messy landscape of bogs, boulders and one collapsed bridge, beneath a sun that arcs from dawn to dusk to show that the work lasts hours. It never lets go of the rolled blueprint it carries, stamped GOAL: BUILD THIS WEBSITE — a destination flag, not a question — and from its belt hang its tools, drawn literally: a terminal window, a browser window, and a magnifying lens for viewing images. Stone waymarkers repeat along the trail in an unbroken loop reading PLAN, ACT, CHECK, CORRECT. At the collapsed bridge the path visibly doubles back before a detour is found, recovering from failure; midway, the robot pauses to study a screenshot of its own half-built site, a red flaw circled on it, an arrow curving back along the trail to fix what it has seen. The trail ends at a gleaming, finished website on a plinth beside a stack of coins — the long, messy, multi-step journey being what valuable work actually looks like — while beyond the end flag the path continues faintly toward a glowing horizon, where tiny figures of engineers are still laying paving stones at the frontier of AI development.
